blocks.content: Prometheus extends observability far beyond what the kubectl tools covered so far in this module offer, scraping and storing metrics over time, enabling real dashboards and alerting, not just a live snapshot.
Running inside a Kubernetes cluster, Prometheus continuously scrapes metrics from Pods and Services, and, critically, stores that data over time, not just the current moment.

blocks.alt: Continuous scraping, with real history retained, not just a passing snapshot

blocks.content: 2. The Direct Contrast With Metrics Server
blocks.text: 2. The Direct Contrast With Metrics Server

blocks.content: This is exactly the distinction flagged back in the Autoscaling module's Metrics Server topic, Metrics Server is deliberately lightweight, real-time only, with no history at all, Prometheus is the real, historical monitoring solution that gap pointed toward.

blocks.alt: The exact gap Metrics Server explicitly left open, now filled by a real monitoring system

blocks.content: 3. ServiceMonitor: How It Finds What to Scrape
blocks.text: 3. ServiceMonitor: How It Finds What to Scrape

blocks.content: In a Kubernetes-specific setup, a ServiceMonitor object tells Prometheus which Services to actually scrape metrics from, a Kubernetes-native way of configuring targets, rather than manually listing them.

blocks.alt: A Kubernetes-native way of telling Prometheus exactly what to watch

blocks.content:
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: ServiceMonitor
metadata:
  name: my-app-monitor
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: my-app
  endpoints:
    - port: metrics

blocks.content: 4. Time-Series Data Enables Real Dashboards and Alerting
blocks.text: 4. Time-Series Data Enables Real Dashboards and Alerting

blocks.content: Because Prometheus retains history as genuine time-series data, it enables things a real-time-only tool simply cannot: trend graphs, alerting rules based on sustained conditions, and dashboards showing how metrics evolved, not just their current value.

blocks.alt: Trends, alerting, and dashboards, all requiring real retained history to work

blocks.content: This topic covers Prometheus specifically in a Kubernetes context, full mechanical depth (PromQL, alerting rules, exporters) is covered in the dedicated Monitoring & Logging category.

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Prometheus scrapes and stores metrics over time, exactly filling the historical gap Metrics Server deliberately leaves open, using ServiceMonitor to discover what to scrape.
Retained time-series data is what enables real dashboards and alerting, full mechanical depth on Prometheus itself lives in the Monitoring & Logging category.
